blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Bathroom Renovation Cost in Geelong in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the real costs of bathroom renovations in Geelong for 2026, including plumbing expenses, fixture options, and tips to maximise your budget with a licensed Geelong plumber.
body: Planning a bathroom renovation in Geelong? One of the first questions homeowners ask is how much it will actually cost. In 2026, bathroom renovation prices in Geelong typically range from $8,000 for a basic refresh to $25,000 or more for a complete luxury transformation. The final price depends on several factors including the size of your bathroom, the quality of fixtures and finishes you select, the complexity of the plumbing work required, and whether any structural changes are needed. At Equality Plumbing, we have completed hundreds of bathroom renovations across Geelong, Belmont, Waurn Ponds, and surrounding suburbs, and we know exactly what goes into a realistic budget.

The size of your bathroom is the most significant factor affecting renovation costs in Geelong. A small ensuite of around four square metres will naturally cost less to renovate than a large main bathroom spanning eight to ten square metres. Larger bathrooms require more materials, more tiling, and often more complex plumbing layouts. Geelong homes, particularly those in older suburbs like Belmont and Newtown, may also have existing plumbing that needs updating to meet current Australian standards. This can add to the overall cost but is essential for compliance and long-term reliability. Your plumber should always conduct a thorough assessment before providing a detailed, fixed-price quote.

Fixture and finish selections dramatically influence your bathroom renovation budget in Geelong. A basic renovation using standard ceramic tiles, a standard vanity, and a basic toilet suite might cost between $8,000 and $12,000. Mid-range options with quality porcelain tiles, a stone-top vanity, and branded fixtures typically fall between $12,000 and $18,000. For a premium renovation featuring floor-to-ceiling designer tiles, freestanding bathtubs, rainfall showers, and high-end tapware, expect to invest $18,000 to $25,000 or more. At Equality Plumbing, we work with Geelong homeowners at every budget level to deliver beautiful results without compromising on quality or compliance.

The plumbing-specific costs in your Geelong bathroom renovation deserve careful attention. Relocating plumbing fixtures such as moving a toilet, shower, or basin to a different position is one of the most expensive aspects of a renovation because it involves cutting into floors and walls, rerouting pipework, and ensuring everything complies with Australian Plumbing Code AS/NZS 3500. Even seemingly small changes like upgrading from a shower over bath to a walk-in shower require modifications to drainage and supply lines. A licensed plumber like Equality Plumbing ensures all work meets strict Geelong council requirements and Australian safety standards, protecting your investment long-term.

Geelong's unique climate also plays a role in bathroom renovation planning. The region experiences cool, damp winters and warm summers, which means proper ventilation and waterproofing are critical to prevent mould and moisture damage. Australian Standard AS 3740 governs waterproofing requirements, and non-compliant waterproofing can void your home insurance. Additionally, older Geelong homes in areas like East Geelong, Hamlyn Heights, and Norlane may have ageing galvanised or lead pipes that should be replaced during a renovation. While this adds to the upfront cost, it prevents future leaks, improves water pressure, and increases your property value over time.

To keep your Geelong bathroom renovation on budget, start by prioritising what matters most to you. If the layout works well, keeping plumbing in the same positions will save thousands of dollars. Invest in quality tapware and a reliable hot water system rather than spending excessively on tiles you can update later. Always request a detailed, itemised quote from your plumber so you understand exactly where every dollar is going. At Equality Plumbing, we provide transparent, fixed-price quotes for all Geelong bathroom renovations, so there are never any nasty surprises. Contact us today for a free consultation and let us help you plan your dream bathroom.

blogPosts.title: Signs You Need Emergency Plumbing in Geelong Before It's Too Late
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn to recognise the critical warning signs of plumbing emergencies in your Geelong home, from burst pipes to gas leaks, and know exactly when to call for help.
body: Plumbing emergencies can strike any Geelong home at any time, often when you least expect them. A burst pipe, a gas leak, or a severely blocked sewer can cause thousands of dollars in damage within minutes if not addressed immediately. Knowing the warning signs of a plumbing emergency can mean the difference between a quick, affordable fix and a catastrophic property disaster. At Equality Plumbing, we provide 24-hour emergency plumbing services across Geelong, Werribee, Lorne, and surrounding suburbs. In this guide, we walk you through the most common signs that you need to call an emergency plumber straight away before the situation worsens.

One of the most obvious signs you need emergency plumbing in Geelong is visible water leaking from pipes or fixtures. If you notice water pooling on your floor, dripping from your ceiling, or spraying from a pipe, you need immediate professional help. Burst pipes are particularly common in Geelong during winter when overnight temperatures drop and pipes in older homes in Belmont, Newtown, or East Geelong can freeze and crack. Even a small, steady drip can waste over 20,000 litres of water per year and cause significant structural damage, mould growth, and rotting timber. Turn off your main water valve immediately and call Equality Plumbing for urgent assistance across the Geelong region.

A gas leak is the most dangerous plumbing emergency you can face in your Geelong home. If you smell rotten eggs or hear a hissing sound near your gas appliances, stove, or hot water system, evacuate your household immediately and call your gas provider from a safe distance. Never use electrical switches, light matches, or operate any ignition source if you suspect a gas leak. Once you are safe, contact a licensed gas fitter like Equality Plumbing. Gas leaks can cause explosions, carbon monoxide poisoning, and serious health risks. We are fully licensed for gas fitting services across Geelong and can respond quickly to make your home safe again.

Severely blocked drains and overflowing toilets are another critical emergency that requires immediate professional attention in Geelong. If multiple drains in your home are backing up simultaneously, this usually indicates a blockage in your main sewer line. Raw sewage backing up into your property is not only unpleasant but poses serious health hazards to your family. Common causes include tree root intrusion, which is particularly prevalent in older Geelong suburbs with established gardens, as well as grease buildup and foreign objects in the pipes. Equality Plumbing uses CCTV drain cameras to quickly diagnose the issue and high-pressure jet blasters to clear even the most stubborn blockages.

A failing hot water system is another situation that often demands emergency plumbing attention in Geelong. If your hot water system is leaking, making unusual noises, or producing rusty water, it could be close to complete failure. In Geelong's cool winters, going without hot water is more than just an inconvenience. A leaking hot water tank can also cause substantial water damage to your property if left unattended. Signs of imminent failure include puddles around the base of the unit, inconsistent water temperature, and strange banging or rumbling sounds. Equality Plumbing provides emergency hot water system repairs and replacements across Geelong, Belmont, Waurn Ponds, and all surrounding areas.

When a plumbing emergency strikes in your Geelong home, the first step is to shut off the relevant isolation valve if it is safe to do so. For gas leaks, leave the property immediately. For burst pipes, turn off the main water supply valve. Avoid attempting complex repairs yourself as this can lead to further damage or personal injury. Call a licensed emergency plumber who can provide fast, professional assistance. Equality Plumbing is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week for emergency callouts across Geelong, Werribee, Lorne, Torquay, and surrounding suburbs. We prioritise urgent situations to protect your home and family.

Choosing the right emergency plumber in Geelong is crucial when every minute counts. Look for a fully licensed, insured professional with local knowledge and proven fast response times. Avoid unlicensed operators who may do more harm than good to your property. At Equality Plumbing, Jaime Woollett and our team have over seven years of experience handling plumbing emergencies throughout the Geelong region. We provide transparent pricing even for emergency callouts, so you know what to expect before any work begins. Save our number, 0432 030 902, in your phone now so you are prepared if a plumbing emergency strikes your Geelong home at any hour.

blogPosts.title: Gas Fitting Safety Tips Every Geelong Homeowner Should Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Essential gas fitting safety advice for Geelong homeowners, covering leak detection, Australian Standards compliance, and when to call a licensed gas fitter for your property.
body: Gas is one of the most efficient and popular energy sources in Australian homes, and many Geelong households rely on gas for cooking, heating, and hot water. However, gas appliances and installations come with serious safety responsibilities that every homeowner must understand. Faulty gas work, poorly maintained appliances, and undetected leaks can lead to explosions, carbon monoxide poisoning, and house fires. As a fully licensed gas fitter serving Geelong, Werribee, Lorne, and surrounding suburbs, Equality Plumbing has put together this comprehensive guide to help you keep your family safe. Understanding gas fitting safety is not optional - it is essential for every Geelong homeowner.

Geelong homes commonly use gas for a range of appliances including cooktops, ovens, gas log fires, space heaters, and hot water systems. Each of these appliances requires proper installation by a licensed gas fitter to operate safely and efficiently. In Geelong's cooler months, gas heaters and fires see heavy use, making regular safety checks even more important. Older Geelong homes in suburbs like East Geelong, Hamlyn Heights, and Norlane may have ageing gas infrastructure that needs upgrading to meet current Australian Standards. If your home was built before the 1990s, it is worth having your gas lines and connections inspected by a qualified professional to ensure ongoing safety.

Knowing the signs of a gas leak can save lives in your Geelong home. The most common indicator is the smell of rotten eggs, which is actually an additive called mercaptan that gas suppliers include specifically to help people detect leaks. Other warning signs include a hissing or whistling sound near gas appliances or connections, dead or dying vegetation near underground gas lines, and unexpected increases in your gas bills without any change in usage. Physical symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, nausea, and difficulty breathing when gas appliances are running can indicate dangerous carbon monoxide buildup. If you notice any of these signs, evacuate immediately and call Equality Plumbing.

Australian gas safety is governed by strict regulations under AS/NZS 5601, which sets out the requirements for gas installations in residential and commercial properties. All gas fitting work in Geelong must be carried out by a licensed gas fitter, and the work must comply with these Australian Standards at all times. Geelong councils also require that gas installations are certified and may require inspection for new builds and major renovations. Using an unlicensed person for gas work is not only illegal under Victorian law but also extremely dangerous to your household. Equality Plumbing holds full gas fitting licences and ensures every installation meets or exceeds Australian Standards.

There are many situations where you should call a licensed gas fitter in Geelong rather than attempting any work yourself. If you smell gas, have a suspected leak, need a new gas appliance installed, or want to convert from electric to gas, always use a licensed professional. Additionally, if you are renovating your Geelong kitchen or bathroom and the project involves moving or adding gas lines, a licensed gas fitter must handle the work by law. Even seemingly simple tasks like connecting a new cooktop or replacing a gas flexible hose require proper licensing and certification. Equality Plumbing services all gas fitting needs across Geelong, Belmont, Waurn Ponds, and surrounding areas.

For Geelong homeowners planning new builds or renovations, gas fitting should be considered early in the design process. Proper planning ensures that gas lines are routed efficiently, appliances are positioned for optimal performance, and all work complies with Australian Standards from the outset. Whether you are building a new home in Torquay, adding an extension in Ocean Grove, or renovating a kitchen in central Geelong, involving a licensed gas fitter early saves time and money. Equality Plumbing works closely with builders, renovators, and homeowners across the Geelong region to design and install gas systems that are safe, efficient, and built to last for decades to come.

Regular maintenance is the key to ongoing gas safety in your Geelong home. Have your gas appliances serviced annually by a qualified technician, and ensure that gas detectors and carbon monoxide alarms are installed and functioning correctly throughout your property. Keep the area around gas appliances clear and well-ventilated, and never use outdoor gas appliances indoors under any circumstances. If you are a Geelong landlord, you have legal obligations under Victorian tenancy laws to ensure all gas installations and appliances in your rental properties are safe and compliant. Equality Plumbing offers comprehensive gas safety inspections and maintenance services across Geelong, Werribee, Lorne, and all surrounding suburbs to keep your property and tenants safe.

blogPosts.title: How to Unclog a Blocked Drain in Geelong: DIY vs Professional Help
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to clearing blocked drains in Geelong homes, comparing DIY solutions with professional drain clearing methods including CCTV inspection and high-pressure jetting.
body: Blocked drains are one of the most common plumbing problems faced by Geelong homeowners, and they can quickly escalate from a minor inconvenience to a serious property issue if not addressed promptly. Slow-draining sinks, gurgling toilets, and foul odours are all telltale signs that a blockage is developing in your drain system. While some minor blockages can be resolved with simple DIY methods, others require professional equipment and expertise. In this guide, we walk Geelong residents through the most effective DIY techniques, explain when it is time to call a professional plumber, and highlight the unique drainage challenges specific to the Geelong region.

Understanding what causes blocked drains in Geelong homes is the first step towards prevention and effective treatment. The most common culprits include grease and fat buildup from kitchen sinks, hair and soap scum in bathroom drains, tree root intrusion into underground sewer lines, foreign objects flushed down toilets, and leaves or debris blocking outdoor stormwater drains. In older Geelong suburbs like Belmont, East Geelong, and Hamlyn Heights, ageing clay sewer pipes are particularly vulnerable to root intrusion from established trees. Heavy rainfall, which Geelong experiences regularly during winter and spring, can also overwhelm drainage systems and worsen existing blockages throughout the region.

For minor blockages in your Geelong home, there are several DIY methods you can try before calling a plumber. The humble plunger is often the first line of defence - create a tight seal over the drain and use firm, consistent plunging motions to dislodge the blockage. A drain snake or wire coat hanger can be used to hook out hair and debris from shower and basin drains. Pouring a mixture of baking soda followed by white vinegar can help break down minor grease buildup, followed by flushing with boiling water. These methods work for surface-level blockages but will not resolve deeper issues in your Geelong property's main sewer or stormwater drain lines.

There are clear signs that a blocked drain in your Geelong home has gone beyond what DIY methods can fix. If multiple drains in your property are affected simultaneously, this usually indicates a blockage in your main sewer line rather than an individual drain. Foul sewer odours throughout your home, water backing up from multiple fixtures, and gurgling sounds from drains when using water are all warning signs of a serious blockage. Sewage backing up into your property is a health hazard that requires immediate professional attention. If any of these symptoms occur in your Geelong home, contact Equality Plumbing immediately for fast, effective drain clearing services across the region.

Professional drain clearing in Geelong uses advanced technology to diagnose and resolve blockages quickly and permanently. At Equality Plumbing, we begin with a CCTV drain camera inspection, which allows us to see exactly what is causing the blockage and where it is located within your drain system. This is far more effective than guesswork and prevents unnecessary excavation of your Geelong property. For most blockages, we use high-pressure water jetting, which blasts through grease, tree roots, and debris at pressures up to 5,000 PSI. This method is highly effective for Geelong's older clay sewer systems and provides a thorough clean that helps prevent future blockages from forming.

Geelong's unique characteristics present specific drainage challenges that homeowners should be aware of. The region's clay soils expand and contract with moisture changes, which can shift and crack underground pipes over time. Many older Geelong suburbs have mature trees with aggressive root systems that commonly infiltrate sewer lines through tiny cracks and joints. Additionally, Geelong's proximity to the coast means that salt air can accelerate corrosion in metal drainage components. Properties in low-lying areas such as parts of Belmont and Newtown are also more prone to stormwater drainage issues during heavy rain events. Understanding these local factors helps Geelong homeowners take proactive steps to protect their drainage systems year-round.

Preventing blocked drains in your Geelong home is always better than dealing with emergency repairs and costly property damage. Avoid pouring cooking oil, grease, or food scraps down kitchen sinks, use drain screens to catch hair in showers and basins, never flush wipes or sanitary products, and keep trees trimmed away from sewer lines where possible. Schedule a CCTV drain inspection every few years, particularly if your Geelong home has mature trees or ageing clay pipes in the ground. Equality Plumbing offers comprehensive drain maintenance services across Geelong, Werribee, Lorne, and surrounding suburbs to keep your plumbing flowing smoothly. Call us today on 0432 030 902 to book your drain inspection.
